html:
Angkor Borei, in southern Cambodia, was a walled city of the early centuries CE, perhaps a capital of Funan, the first major state of the region. Canals linked it across the delta to the port of Óc Eo.

Funan grew rich on the sea trade between India and China, and took up Indian religions, writing and kingship. The oldest dated inscription in Khmer, from 611, was found here; see Khmer script.

Funan gave way to the inland state of Chenla in the 6th century, centred at Sambor Prei Kuk. Angkor Borei's museum keeps statues of Vishnu and the Buddha from its golden age.
